last_run.broken_assumption: HumanityAI should adopt frontier architecture ideas because they sound conceptually stronger. Instead, competing workflows should be tested head-to-head before structural adoption.

strongest_ideas.name: Blind historical architecture backtest
strongest_ideas.idea: Compare the current supply-first problem/evidence workflow against the proposed decision-centric lifecycle on the same historical public-interest decisions, with a strict information cutoff and post-outcome reveal only after both arms freeze recommendations and forecasts.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: The project has started generating architectural hypotheses but lacks a method for experimentally deciding whether one architecture actually improves decision-relevant analysis. This turns architecture selection itself into a falsifiable process.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Creates evidence for or against the decision-centric architecture, reduces path dependence and persuasive-story bias, and could become a general pattern for testing future HumanityAI workflow changes before promotion into core structure.
failure_modes: Historical cases can leak hindsight information into supposedly pre-outcome analysis.
Case selection can favor one workflow.
Later outcomes are confounded and do not perfectly identify decision quality.
A decision-centric workflow may look better merely because it produces more structured documentation.
Small samples may produce noisy conclusions.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Evaluation explicitly includes affected groups and rights/distribution considerations rather than treating decision-owner utility as the sole objective.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High; the test is retrospective and additive and changes no protected governance or security structure.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Select three historical cases with preregistered information cutoff dates, run independent current-workflow and decision-centric arms without post-cutoff evidence, freeze outputs, then reveal later evidence and compare on predeclared multidimensional measures.

rejected_or_deferred: Promote the decision-to-outcome lifecycle directly into core schemas before testing it: too much path dependence for an unvalidated architecture idea.

Judge the experiment only by whether the historical outcome matched the recommendation: outcomes are stochastic and confounded, so calibration, uncertainty, evidence-gap discovery, rights considerations and reviewer usefulness must remain separate dimensions.
Use the same agent context for both arms: cross-contamination would make the comparison weak; separate contexts are preferred when practical.
Run live real-world decisions first: unnecessary risk before a retrospective test establishes information value.
implemented: Added agent/frontier_experiments/decision_workflow_backtest_001.json as a concrete low-risk experiment specification.
last_run.recommended_next_test: Preregister three historical cases and their cutoff dates before analysis. If the decision-centric arm does not repeatedly add material decision value at acceptable review cost, do not promote it into core architecture.

notes: Frontier state records conceptual experiments, not authority. Ideas may exceed current execution permissions; human-review boundaries remain governed by security/policy.json.
